substitutionTest.note: Standing procedure, run before any pairing test: 11 of 18 testable baseline sentences of four or more words survive verbatim in the current text after punctuation normalization. The count is nonzero, so the section is not in substitution mode and the pairing tests apply. The shortfall is dominated by the recorded coda-scaffold removal, the linked reading-path lines, and ledger-bounded sentences whose interiors changed by one modality word.

findings.summary: The chamber's coda scaffold is not restored, and its first two lines were content.

evidence.baseline: This is the human condition: to hold more than one life can spend, and to ache for the place to spend it. This is the work: to build the nest where it can be spent together.
evidence.shipped: A human life can hold more capacity than it finds occasion to spend. The work comes down to building places where people can become, together, what none could become alone.

findings.authorizedBy: The voice card's known weak passages, and the semantic review's record of the coda removal.
findings.diagnosis: Coda scaffold not restored. The baseline closes this chamber with a divider, two italic address lines, the isolated line That is why, and a fourth italic line beginning That is why. The Volume VI voice card lists any return of the repeated divider plus That is why coda among its known weak passages, and the semantic review records the pass's removal of the scaffold as a structural repair. The address lines also tell the reader what they have felt, waited for, or were made to become, which is the defect CTD-0091 was opened for and which the corpus card forbids outright. The scaffold is therefore left removed. Where a coda carried content rather than performance, that content is restored into the chamber body. The first two coda lines here state the volume's thesis rather than perform intimacy, and the pass rewrote them into the chamber body, where the card now protects the result verbatim.

findings.summary: The three-act line lost its ordinals.

evidence.baseline: Recognition is the first act, belonging the second, stewardship the last.
evidence.shipped: Recognition opens, belonging holds, and stewardship carries forward.

findings.diagnosis: The ordinals are the sequence, which is the whole content of the line inside a refrain built of definitions. Opens, holds, carries forward substitutes three verbs for an order and loses the claim that stewardship comes last.

findings.summary: The nest's arrival lost its address and its history.

evidence.baseline: That is all the nest has ever been, the smallest structure in which the largest becoming can start. Everything in these six volumes was only trying to help you find it, and to say to you, before you began, why it was worth the building.
evidence.shipped: The nest is the smallest structure in which a larger becoming can start. These six volumes offer reasons to find or build one.

findings.authorizedBy: Catalog 4.16, performed intimacy, applied to the second person.
findings.diagnosis: The largest becoming is the volume's phrase and a larger becoming is a hedge on a superlative that the nest image earns. To say to you, before you began, why it was worth the building is the closing beat of Part One and the only place the volume states its own purpose to a reader.

findings.summary: The coda's closing hand-over, And now it is yours, was neither folded into the body nor recorded as removed.
findings.authorizedBy: The coda scaffold removal, which covers the divider, the address lines, and the That is why pair, and which generation A extended to this line without recording it.
findings.diagnosis: The line is content, not scaffold: it assigns nothing to the reader and it is the same sentence that closes The Largest Nest, so the baseline hands the nest over twice, once at each part's close. The Largest Nest's record already ruled the sentence safe under the autonomy standard. Cutting the first instance silently halved an earned return. Restored as the body's closing line by this audit and flagged for the author, who may prefer the echo only at the volume's end.

Restored as the body's closing line and recorded as F5. Ledger swept for the sentence: no item governs it, and this volume's record for The Largest Nest already adjudicated the same sentence as handing forward rather than assigning.
R-CAUTIOUS-HALF. The refrain lines survive committing, with might become bounded at the width the chamber VIII decision names.

R-REFRAIN-COST. The divider plus That is why coda is a volume-wide refrain, removed once by one decision. The anchor record v06-the-current carries the refrain finding with its count of eleven; this chamber cites the anchor rather than repeating the analysis. This chamber's first two coda lines were content and are folded into the body's closing pair, as the anchor's fold audit records.

R-PAIRED-DELETION. Term sweep run over the section's distinctive named terms against the baseline and the current corpus. No cross-reference was restored at one end; no dependency blocks. The restored line's pair is The Largest Nest's close; both ends now stand, restoring the baseline's echo at the two part closes.

R-DEIXIS and R-TENSE checked against the baseline's demonstratives and verb forms. Nothing fires. R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD. No claim named in an open canon query was cut from this section by this audit or left unrecorded by generation A.

openQuestions: The protected line Coherence is the current. Purpose is the pathway. Providence is the loom. is declared as one quoted string. In both the baseline and the current source those are three separate display lines inside the Smallest Nest sequence, so the string as quoted has never appeared in the manuscript. All three sentences are present verbatim and in order. Running them together would destroy a protected display device, so the card's quotation is what needs correcting.

Voice card exemplar anchors. The Volume VI card lists opening anchors drawn from the compressed pass rather than from the baseline, so a faithful re-render displaces some of them. Four of the card's five protected lines were also authored by the pass and do not exist in the baseline at all; all four are kept verbatim. The card needs re-preparation against the re-rendered source, and that is a card revision the author should authorise.

And now it is yours is restored at the close of Part One, rebuilding the baseline's echo with The Largest Nest. The scaffold decision never named the line, so the restoration follows the baseline's authority on prose, but the author may prefer the hand-over to sound only once, at the volume's end. One cut settles it if so.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus card, the volume-06 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The chamber contains the volume's only case of a coda line that was thesis rather than performance, and the pass handled it correctly: it moved the content into the body before deleting the scaffold. The card then protected the rewritten sentence, which is why the re-render keeps the pass's wording here and the baseline's everywhere else in the chamber.
